links.outcome: Strict under-triage of KTAS 1-2 cases predicted as levels 4-5, and over-triage
links.effect: Fine-tuned model strict under-triage 0.65%; within-one-level agreement 97.13%; fewer extreme errors and lower under-triage than XGBoost in selected high-acuity groups, at the cost of higher over-triage.
links.quote: However, the fine-tuned model showed fewer extreme errors and lower strict under-triage in selected high-acuity groups, at the cost of higher over-triage.

links.outcome: Overall triage performance of fine-tuned LLM versus structured-data XGBoost comparator
links.effect: LLM accuracy 58.60%, macro-F1 0.417, QWK 0.535 vs XGBoost accuracy 69.40%, macro-F1 0.618, QWK 0.651; LLM had a safer error profile.
links.quote: The structured-data comparator showed higher overall performance, with an accuracy of 69.40%, a macro-F1 score of 0.618, and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.651.

links.outcome: Lack of external and prospective validation of the model
links.effect: Single-center retrospective benchmark; authors state external and prospective validation are necessary before clinical implementation.
links.quote: External and prospective validation will be necessary before clinical implementation.

unlisted_practices: Safety-oriented reward design in reinforcement fine-tuning (GRPO) to reduce under-triage

screen.reason: The study is a retrospective benchmark evaluating a fine-tuned small language model (Qwen3-8B) with a safety-oriented reward design against an XGBoost model on pediatric emergency triage data. It evaluates model accuracy and error profiles (safety metrics like strict under-triage) rather than testing an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
